newsitem.title: USA: APICS business outlook index rose to 51.8 in Dec.
newsitem.headline: APICS business outlook index rose to 51.8 in Dec.

text.p: The American Production and Inventory Control Society (APICS) business outlook index rebounded to 51.8 in December from 46.8 in November.
The current component rose to 51.2 from 48.3 during the same period, with the future component up to 52.4 from 45.3.
A reading of 50 indicates neutral sentiment, APICS said.
"Last month, the index showed new orders dropping sharply, which is precisely what happened," APICS said. "However, orders rebounded somewhat in December; the decline last month was only temporary."
The APICS index is compiled monthly from a survey of manufacturing firms and is calculated by averaging respondents' ratings of current and future conditions.
Two of four current components rose in December. Shipments jumped to 59.5 from 46.7 the month before and employment hit the 54.5 mark, up from 43.7.
Production and inventories components fell during the month. Inventories dropped to 41.0 from 50.8 and production slipped to 50.0 from 52.1.
Three of four future components gained in November, APICS said. Only the production planning component fell, to 47.5 in December from 49.3 the month before.
Among the gainers, the new orders component rose to 55.3 from 41.9, unfilled orders rose to 49.7 from 46.6 and inventory/sales ratio jumped to 57.1 from 43.3, APICS said.
